title: South Indian cotton yarn sentiment improves, Mumbai prices rise
content:
South India’s cotton market firmed, with Mumbai cotton yarn prices rising ₹3–5 (~$0.03–0.05) per kg as costlier cotton lifted spinning mills’ sentiment, while Tiruppur held steady.
Traders expect downstream demand to improve after Diwali, though payment constraints and possible yarn dispatch disruptions remain concerns.
Gujarat cotton gained ₹100–200 per candy on slow arrivals after erratic rainfall.

title: Bangladesh’s $9.17 bn non-cotton shift meets a $2.43 bn input bill
content:
Non-cotton apparel made up 30.7 per cent of Bangladesh’s $29.91 billion garment exports in January to September 2026, but TexPro data show uneven diversification.
Selected fibre, yarn and fabric imports rose 4.6 per cent to $2.43 billion in H1, with China supplying 81.3 per cent.
Energy shortages, woven gaps and planned polyester-chip capacity will shape where value is captured.

title: India to fund micro & small exporters' certification under EPM: Goyal
content:
India will cover the full cost of expensive certifications for micro and small enterprises under the Export Promotion Mission, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said. 
Support will also cover EU compliance, including CBAM and EUDR, helping exporters ease testing, certification, emissions-monitoring and traceability costs and improve global competitiveness.

title: US cotton export sales surge 36%, Vietnam leads buying
content:
US Upland cotton export sales rose 36 per cent to 199,600 RB in the week ended October 15, with shipments up 40 per cent to 196,400 RB, USDA data showed.
Vietnam led purchases at 94,500 RB, followed by Bangladesh, Turkiye, Pakistan and India, as Asian textile-producing markets drove the rebound.
Pima cotton demand weakened, with sales down 81 per cent and exports down 28 per cent.

title: Bangladesh apparel exports to EU fall 11.4%: What drives the drop?
content:
TexPro data show Bangladesh apparel export value for HS 61 and HS 62 to EU destinations fell 11.43 per cent in January–August 2026.
Values declined 4.31 per cent to the United States, 0.61 per cent to the United Kingdom and 7.69 per cent worldwide.
Eurostat data show EU apparel imports from Bangladesh fell 11.67 per cent; buyers should prepare for the EU’s post-transition preference framework.

title: US’ Deckers Brands' Q2 profit rises 17% as Hoka, UGG expand
content:
Deckers Brands has raised its FY27 diluted earnings per share outlook after second-quarter earnings exceeded expectations, supported by disciplined marketplace management and expense control. 
Second-quarter net sales rose 3.5 per cent to $1.48 billion, while net income increased 17 per cent to $313.1 million. 
Tariff refunds lifted margins and EPS, as Hoka and UGG both delivered sales growth.
